questions.q: Notepad, the basic Windows text editor, saves files as:
questions.solution: Notepad writes plain text with no bold/italic formatting - its default extension is .txt. Formatted text needs WordPad or a word processor.
questions.shortcut: No formatting = Notepad; any option promising fonts/bold is WordPad/Word territory.

questions.q: A modem's function is to:
options: Convert digital signals to analog and back
questions.solution: MOdulator-DEModulator: it turns the computer's digital bits into analog carrier tones (and vice versa) for transmission over telephone/cable plant. Routing is a router; rule-filtering is a firewall.
questions.shortcut: Digital <-> analog conversion is the modem's whole identity.

questions.q: Which of the following is a non-impact printer?
questions.solution: Laser printers form images with electrostatic toner - no physical strike - so they are non-impact (as are inkjet and thermal). Dot matrix and daisy wheel strike an inked ribbon.
questions.shortcut: Impact family is short: dot matrix + daisy wheel. Almost every other printer is non-impact.

questions.q: Which protocol is normally used by live audio/video streaming where speed matters more than perfect delivery?
questions.solution: UDP is connectionless with no retransmission overhead, so realtime media, VoIP and gaming prefer it. TCP guarantees ordered delivery (web, mail, downloads).

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

He said to me, "Please lend me your pen."
options: He requested me to lend him my pen.
He requested me to lend me your pen.
He ordered me to lend him my pen.
He said to me please to lend him my pen.
questions.solution: Please → **requested**; to lend + him (speaker) + my (listener). B leaves both pronouns direct; C mismatches tone (ordered for a request); D has no sentence structure.
questions.shortcut: please sets the verb: requested; then him + my.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

Hardly **I had reached** the office when the fire alarm went off.
questions.solution: *Hardly* opening the sentence forces auxiliary-first order: **had I reached** (past perfect pairs with *when*). 'Did I reached' pairs *did* with a past form; 'I had reach' keeps statement order and breaks the participle.
questions.shortcut: Hardly/Scarcely at sentence start → had + subject + participle.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

She is not capable ___ handling so much pressure at work.
questions.solution: The fixed collocation is **capable of** + V-ing. *capable for / in / to* are not standard.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

Not only the students but also the wardens **was** honoured at the function.
questions.solution: The nearness rule applies to not only…but also too: the nearer subject *the wardens* is plural → **were** honoured. 'Has been' would also break the passive plural.

questions.q: The **Dronacharya Award** is given for excellence in —
questions.solution: Instituted in **1985**, the Dronacharya Award honours **sports coaches**. The Arjuna Award is for sportspersons.
questions.shortcut: Drona was the guru (coach) of Arjuna — coach vs player.

questions.q: The Commonwealth Games 2026 were hosted by —
questions.solution: Glasgow, Scotland (23 July – 2 August 2026) — Scotland's fourth time hosting after Edinburgh 1970 & 1986 and Glasgow 2014. Birmingham hosted 2022.
questions.shortcut: Glasgow repeat: 2014 → 2026, stepping in as revised host.

questions.q: Which metal is a liquid at normal room temperature?
questions.solution: **Mercury** is the metal that is liquid at room temperature. **Bromine** is also liquid but is a **non-metal**. Gallium melts at about 30 °C — in the palm — but is solid at a normal room temperature of about 25 °C.
questions.shortcut: Liquid metal = Hg; liquid non-metal = Br.

questions.q: The **Santosh Trophy** is associated with —
questions.solution: The **Santosh Trophy** is India's national football championship for state teams, first held in 1941. The Ranji Trophy is its cricket counterpart.

questions.q: The price of an article is first increased by 20% and then decreased by 20%. The net change in price is:

questions.solution: $a^3 - b^3 = (a-b)(a^2 + ab + b^2)$, so the value is simply $a - b = 15.2 - 5.2 = 10$.

questions.q: If $\tan\theta=\dfrac{3}{4}$, the value of $\dfrac{\sin\theta+\cos\theta}{\sin\theta-\cos\theta}$ is:
questions.solution:
Divide numerator and denominator by $\cos\theta$:

$\dfrac{\tan\theta+1}{\tan\theta-1}=\dfrac{\frac34+1}{\frac34-1}=\dfrac{7/4}{-1/4}=-7$.
questions.shortcut: Divide through by $\cos\theta$: $(t+1)/(t-1)$ with $t=\frac34$ → $-7$. (Same trick works for any sin/cos ratio expression.)
questions.pattern: divide by cos to use tan

questions.q: The total surface area of a cuboid of dimensions $8\text{ cm}\times6\text{ cm}\times4\text{ cm}$ is:
questions.shortcut: Half of 208 is 104 — the bracket sum; double it. Trap: 104 (no doubling).

questions.q: In a group of **80 people, 50 like cricket and 40 like hockey**. What is the **maximum** number of people who like **neither** game?
questions.solution: Neither is largest when the circles cover as few people as possible — hockey fully inside cricket. Then at least one = 50 and neither = 80 − 50 = **30**. 0 is the minimum; 10 is the minimum overlap.

questions.q:
**Statement:** A shop sold 120 shirts in January and 150 shirts in February.

**Conclusions:**
I. The number of shirts sold rose by 25% from January to February.
II. The shop made more profit in February than in January.

Which of the conclusions follow(s) from the statement?
questions.solution: I: rise = (150 − 120) ÷ 120 × 100 = 25% — **follows**. II: profit depends on prices and costs, which are not given; more pieces sold does not prove more profit — **does not follow**. Answer: **only I**.
questions.shortcut: Percentage change is on the old value. Sales ≠ profit.

questions.q: In a certain code, **ZIP is coded 30** (A = 26, B = 25 ... Z = 1). How is **MAP** coded?

Study the pattern and find the missing number.

**Grid 1:** 3, 5, 16  **Grid 2:** 4, 6, 25  **Grid 3:** 5, 7, ?

(Each grid is read left to right as one row.)
questions.solution: Grid 1: 3 × 5 + 1 = 16; grid 2 confirms: 4 × 6 + 1 = 25 ✓. Grid 3: 5 × 7 + 1 = **36**. (35 is the bare product.)
questions.shortcut: Solve grid 1, confirm on grid 2, apply to grid 3.
